network: ValidationRegime::select drops the ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT branch
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/10

## Why

Reviewer's `ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT` bumps assume that operators with stale local chains will catch up "naturally" through tip validation, but `ValidationRegime::select` (`src/network/tip_validation.rs:137`) actively traps them in the 300 s Bootstrap deadline.

Concretely, observed live on `exfer-node-stack` after the v1.10.1 → v1.11.0 upgrade (which bumped `ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT` from 302,400 to 500,000):

| | |
|---|---|
| Local tip when v1.11.0 came up | 463,702 (validated end-to-end under v1.10.x's lower checkpoint) |
| Mainnet tip | 610,087 |
| Gap to catch up | ~146 k headers |
| Selected regime under old logic | Bootstrap (`463,702 < ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT == 500,000`) |
| Bootstrap deadline | 300 s |
| Expected forward-validation work at SteadyState 20/sec | ~11,000 s |
| Observed | Every peer's `TipResponse` failed with `deadline exceeded`, IBD did not advance for 9+ hours |

Forcing `--no-assume-valid` flips the node back into SteadyState (the third branch of `select()`) and unblocks IBD, at the cost of a multi-hour `open_chain` walk on every boot. That's a runtime workaround, not a fix.

## What

Regime selection now depends only on whether we have a local chain (`our_tip_height > 0`), not on how the local tip compares to `ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT`.

\`\`\`rust
pub fn select(our_tip_height: u64, _assume_valid: bool) -> Self {
    if our_tip_height == 0 {
        ValidationRegime::Bootstrap   // path 2b fetches checkpoint header
    } else {
        ValidationRegime::SteadyState // path 2a anchors at our local tip
    }
}
\`\`\`

Rationale: a local tip we built ourselves is always a valid anchor for path 2a regardless of how a future release reclassifies the checkpoint. The only case that genuinely needs path 2b is the fresh-datadir bootstrap where no anchor exists in local storage.

The `assume_valid` parameter is retained for API stability; it's now unused inside `select()`.

## What doesn't change

* `tip == 0` still selects Bootstrap. Path 2b at `sync.rs:7619` still fetches the checkpoint header from a peer and verifies its `block_id` against `ASSUME_VALID_HASH`; `--verify-all` on a fresh node still falls through to the legacy single-header path because no trusted anchor exists.
* `path_2b_usable` checks at `sync.rs:4984` and `sync.rs:7613` keep the same `Bootstrap && assume_valid && cumulative_work_trusted` shape. With the new rule, that combination is reachable only when `tip == 0`, so path 2b is now strictly the fresh-node bootstrap path — which matches its docstring.
* `compute_deadline`, the 300 s / 7200 s floor constants, the rate caps (`VALIDATION_ARGON2_PER_CORE_BOOTSTRAP`, `MAX_VALIDATION_ARGON2_PER_SEC`), and the concurrency caps are untouched.
